about.title: Personal Injury Help in Eureka, California
about.longDescription: Eureka's streets carry a steady flow of local and through traffic, from Broadway Street and Highway 101 to the busier stretches of H Street and I Street near downtown. In the most recent year on record, Humboldt County logged 214 injury collisions in and around the city, leaving 288 people hurt and 4 people dead. Numbers like these represent neighbors, commuters, and families whose routines were interrupted in an instant. If that happened to you or someone you love, sorting out medical bills, insurance calls, and missed work can feel like a full-time job on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who can look at what happened and explain your options. We are not a law firm, and we don't decide your case or offer legal advice ourselves — we simply help you get in front of someone who can. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Reaching out costs nothing and starts the process of finding out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: California's Filing Deadline
items.desc: Most injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the accident. That window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity was involved, so timing matters.

items.title: Shared Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply adjusted to reflect your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That can matter a great deal when an injury affects your daily life long after medical bills stop.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to You
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, which means they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no bill for exploring your options.

items.question: How much time do I have to file a claim in Eureka?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity, like the city or county, was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's wise to act quickly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't eliminated.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Eureka?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along corridors like Broadway Street, Highway 101, H Street, and I Street, with reports tending to peak on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. These are simply reported counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and there's no cost to be connected with an independent attorney. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so they only get paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In most ordinary personal injury cases in California, there is no cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. Every case is different, and an attorney can help explain what factors might affect your specific situation.
